13 The diagram shows the arrangement of atoms in a particular crystal.
Each atom is at the corner of a cube.
kg. The density of the crystal is 9.2  103
The mass of each atom is 3.5  10–25
kg m–3.
What is the shortest distance between the centres of two adjacent atoms?
A
3.8  10–29
m
B
6.2  10–15
m
C
3.4  10–10
m
D
3.0  10–9
m

hints: Notice the diagram shows a simple cubic lattice where each atom sits at the corner of a cube, so the shortest centre-to-centre distance is the side length $a$ of one small cube.
Connect mass and density through $\rho = m/V$ to find the volume $V = a^3$ belonging to one atom using $3.5 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg}$ and $9.2 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
After calculating $V$ in $\text{m}^3$, take the cube root $a = V^{1/3}$ and check the power of ten gives an atomic size near $10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the repeating unit: each atom is at the corner of a cube, so one atom occupies one cube of side $a$ equal to the adjacent-atom spacing.
State the density rule $\rho = m/V$, so volume per atom is $V = m/\rho$.
Substitute values with units: $V = (3.5 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg})/(9.2 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}) \approx 3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$.
Relate this volume to the cube side: $V = a^3$, so $a = V^{1/3}$.
Calculate $a = (3.8 \times 10^{-29})^{1/3} \text{ m} \approx 3.4 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$, with units of length and typical atomic spacing size.

A.explanation: This is the volume occupied by one atom, $3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$, not a length. A cube root is still needed to get atomic spacing.

B.explanation: This is the square root of the volume per atom. Spacing is the side of a cube, so the cube root of the volume must be taken.

C.explanation: Volume per atom divided by density gives $3.8 \times 10^{-29} \text{ m}^3$, whose cube root is about $3.4 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This is about ten times too large and does not follow from $V = m/\rho$ followed by a cube root with the given $3.5 \times 10^{-25} \text{ kg}$ and $9.2 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
